summary: A small wooden rear range tower of 1894 on a keeper's farm west of Victoria, PEI, kept by father and son Wright until 1959.

access.note: Private property near Beach Light Road; grounds and tower closed.

events.note: Electricity installed; Charles Evan Wright's keepership ends
Moved a short distance due to shoreline erosion
Designated under Heritage Lighthouse Protection Act 13 March 2025

keepers.name: Charles L. Wright
keepers.note: Paid $20 for the land, $100 a year salary; $130 in 1910 statement

evidence.supports: 1894 range lights established for Victoria Harbour
evidence.quote: In 1894, two new sets of range lights, the Palmer Range and Wrights Range, were established

evidence.supports: first activated 15 June 1894; rear light in orchard
evidence.quote: When first activated on June 15, 1894
The original Wrights Rear Range Light was located in the corner of an orchard
The structure for the rear light was a square, open-framed, wooden tower whose seaward face was slatted, painted white, and surmounted by a red lantern.
The lack of a separate lantern, with the light instead visible through a sea-facing window, is unusual.
The range light was originally an open frame tower which had white slats on the seaward sides.
Charles L. Wright was appointed keeper of his namesake lights on June 14, 1894, was paid $20 for the land on which the rear light stood, and received an annual salary of $100.
The lighthouse is named for its original keeper Charles L. Wright, on whose land it was built.
Wrights Range Charles Wright June 14, 1894. . . . 130 00
He received an Imperial Long Service Medal for his many years of faithful lightkeeping.
He served through 1935 and was succeeded by his son, Charles Evan Wright, who was keeper until 1959.
His son Charles Evan Wright succeeded him in 1935 and maintained the light until 1959 when electricity was installed.
Edward H. Boswell (1959), Bryce Boswell (1959)
major repairs were undertaken in 1957
A solar panel supplied electricity to the range light prior to it being decommissioned in August 2011.
In 1986 the lighthouse was moved a short distance due to shoreline erosion.
The Coast Guard deactivated Wrights Range in 2011.
Decommissioned in August 2011.
Note that the red range light on the rear tower has been removed.
announced the designation of the Wrights Front Range and Wrights Rear Range Lighthouses under the Heritage Lighthouse Protection Act
The lighthouse is located in a mixed residential and agricultural area at the end of Beach Light Road
The tower is located on private property close to Beach Light Road
Grounds/tower closed.
has submitted a petition for ownership of the lighthouse under the Parks Canada Heritage Lighthouse Program.
overlooking Paul's Bluff and the Northumberland Strait just west of Victoria Harbour
It was constructed without a separate lantern.
The Government of Canada owns the range light.
The lighthouse is owned by the Canadian Coast Guard.

corrections.why: Lighthouse Friends says 2011 and the PEI Lighthouse Society says August 2011; nothing found for 2014.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia says still active; Lighthouse Friends, the PEI Lighthouse Society and the CCG record indicate deactivation in 2011 with the red light removed.
